stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition Snapshot 13w17a in a new single-player Creative-mode Superflat world. Use default controls where possible. The Superflat world, Creative mode, a cow, and reduced render distance are practical choices for creating and unloading the test arrangement without crafting, exploration, combat, or terrain obstacles; the report does not require those exact choices.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected version Snapshot 13w17a; do not use either listed fix version, Minecraft 15w31b or 1.15 Pre-release 1.
Use an unmodified vanilla client with no mods or external server software that could alter entity or chunk-loading behavior.
Create a disposable world because this reproduction deliberately tests historical snapshot behavior.
The executor must be able to use Creative inventory and Creative flight.
Use a leashable animal. This plan selects a cow as a simple representative of the report's stated 'any animals' condition.
Place the test site well away from the initial world-spawn area so spawn-chunk loading is less likely to keep the animal's chunk active.
Perform one unload-and-return cycle initially. The report describes the issue as occurring 'most of the times,' so one clean cycle does not establish that the setup was invalid.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for the exact historical version listed as "Snapshot 13w17a", start it, and wait for the main menu. Do not substitute a later release or either fix version.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and the displayed game version identifies 13w17a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, open More World Options, set World Type to Superflat, and create the world. Leave the seed unspecified because the report supplies no required seed.
steps.success_cue: World generation has started with Creative mode and the Superflat world type selected.

steps.action: Wait without opening another menu until the world is visible, nearby flat terrain has rendered, and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally in a fully rendered area of the Superflat world.

steps.action: Press Esc, select Options, select Video Settings, and click the Render Distance setting until it reads Tiny. Return to the world. The historical Far, Normal, Short, and Tiny render-distance labels and their era-appropriate ranges were externally checked. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Talk%3AServer.properties/Archive_1?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The world is active again and distant terrain is hidden by the short Tiny render distance.

steps.action: Press F3 to open the debug display. Read and record the player's initial X and Z coordinates as spawn-reference coordinates. Ignore Y for the horizontal-distance calculations.
steps.success_cue: The debug display is visible and the initial X and Z values have been recorded.

steps.action: Enter Creative flight by double-tapping the Jump control, whose default key is Space. Hold the Forward control, whose default key is W, and travel horizontally until the current position is at least 320 blocks from the recorded initial position along X, Z, or their combined horizontal displacement.
steps.success_cue: The F3 coordinates show that the player is at least 320 horizontal blocks from the initial position.

steps.action: Descend using the Sneak control, whose default key is Left Shift, until standing on the flat ground. Wait until the local terrain is fully rendered and movement is responsive.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on stable ground at a test site at least 320 blocks from the initial position.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use the Search Items tab if available and place one Fence, one Lead, and one cow spawn egg into separate hotbar slots. In this historical version, use the single wooden item named Fence rather than a modern wood-specific fence name. Close the inventory with E or Esc.
steps.success_cue: A Fence, a Lead, and a cow spawn egg are visible in separate hotbar slots.

steps.action: Select the Fence's hotbar slot using its number key or the mouse wheel. Aim at the top surface of a nearby grass block and press the Use Item control, whose default input is right-click, once to place the fence.
steps.success_cue: One upright fence post is present at the test site.

steps.action: Select the cow spawn egg. Aim at an open grass block approximately 2 to 4 blocks horizontally from the fence and right-click once to spawn a cow.
steps.success_cue: One living cow is present near the fence with an unobstructed path between the cow and fence.

steps.action: Select the Lead in the hotbar, move within interaction range of the cow, aim directly at the cow, and right-click it once to attach the held lead.
steps.success_cue: A lead line visibly connects the player to the cow while the player remains near it.

steps.action: While the cow remains attached to the held lead, walk to the fence, aim directly at the fence post, and right-click the fence once to tie the lead to it.
steps.success_cue: The lead now runs between the cow and the fence, and a lead knot is visible on the fence post.

steps.action: Stop moving for several seconds and confirm only the setup state: the cow remains close to the fence, the lead is visibly attached at both ends, and neither endpoint is near the lead's maximum stretched distance. Do not yet leave the area.
steps.success_cue: A stable cow-to-fence lead arrangement is present before any chunk unloading occurs.

steps.action: With F3 still open, record the fence's approximate X and Z coordinates as the return coordinates. If F3 was closed, press F3 before recording them.
steps.success_cue: The test site's X and Z return coordinates have been recorded.

steps.action: Face directly away from the test site and enter Creative flight by double-tapping Space. Ascend several blocks so fences or minor terrain cannot obstruct horizontal travel.
steps.success_cue: The player is airborne and can travel away from the cow-and-fence test site without ground obstacles.

steps.action: Fly horizontally away from the recorded test-site coordinates. Continue until F3 shows a horizontal displacement of at least 512 blocks from the test site. Do not merely fly upward above the same X and Z position; the player must leave the test area's horizontal chunk-loading range.
steps.exact_input: Hold W until horizontal distance is at least 512 blocks
steps.success_cue: The recorded test site is not visible, and the current X/Z position is at least 512 horizontal blocks from it.

steps.action: Remain at the distant location for at least 10 seconds with the game unpaused. Wait until nearby destination chunks have rendered and player movement responds normally before returning.
steps.success_cue: The player has remained over 512 blocks away for at least 10 unpaused seconds and the destination area is fully responsive.

steps.action: Turn toward the recorded test-site coordinates and fly back horizontally. Use the F3 X and Z values to correct direction as needed, keeping the return coordinates centered as the distance decreases.
steps.exact_input: Hold W and navigate toward the recorded X/Z coordinates
steps.success_cue: The player's horizontal distance from the recorded test site is steadily decreasing.

steps.action: Continue approaching until the terrain at the recorded test-site coordinates transitions from outside the rendered area into view. Do not interact with the cow, fence, ground, or any dropped item during this approach.
steps.success_cue: The block terrain containing the recorded test site has just re-entered rendered view after being taken at least 512 blocks out of range.

steps.action: Stop close enough to view the test site, and wait only until its surrounding terrain has finished rendering and movement responds normally. Do not right-click the animal or fence and do not pick up or break anything; preserve the freshly reloaded state for the Observation Agent.
steps.success_cue: The recorded cow-and-fence test area is fully rendered and responsive after the unload-and-return cycle, with no post-return interaction performed.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just returned from at least 512 blocks away, the chunk containing the previously verified cow-to-fence lead arrangement has re-entered rendered view, surrounding terrain has finished loading, and the player has not interacted with or altered the setup since returning. Begin observation of the freshly reloaded lead arrangement.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, seed, world type, animal species, render distance, exact unload distance, or exact unload duration. Creative mode, Superflat terrain, a cow, Tiny render distance, a site at least 320 blocks from the initial spawn position, a 512-block departure, and a 10-second distant wait are practical execution choices rather than report requirements.

The issue combines multiple possible manifestations after unloading and reloading. This plan reproduces only their common setup and trigger and intentionally does not classify which manifestation, if any, occurred.

The report states that an occurrence happens 'most of the times,' so the behavior is intermittent. If the Observation Agent records no occurrence, a later independent trial may recreate a fresh cow-to-fence attachment and repeat the unload cycle; repeated triggering is not included in the initial plan.
The exact launcher navigation used to expose historical snapshots can vary by launcher release. Regardless of launcher UI, the game process must identify itself as 13w17a before execution continues.

External verification was limited to the historical render-distance labels and approximate era-specific ranges. The Mojira report remains the source for the actual lead attachment and chunk-unload trigger.

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition 1.4.2 in a disposable singleplayer world using the integrated server. Create the setup in Creative mode with cheats enabled, then enter Survival mode for the fall. Do not use a dedicated multiplayer server, because the report explicitly excludes vanilla dedicated-server worlds.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact Java Edition version Minecraft 1.4.2; do not use the listed fix version Minecraft 1.4.3.
Use a new or otherwise disposable singleplayer world so that dying or altering terrain cannot damage a valuable save.

Use default controls or their rebound equivalents: E for inventory, T for chat, Esc for the pause menu, Space for jump/ascend, W for forward movement, left-click for breaking, and right-click for placing blocks.
Enable cheats during world creation so that the player can switch from Creative mode to Survival mode.
Use a normal non-Hardcore world. No seed, dimension, or coordinates are required by the report.
Before the test fall, the player must have full health, no armor equipped, no status effects, and no fall-damage-reducing equipment.
The landing surface must be ordinary solid ground. It must not contain water, ladders, vines, cobwebs, beds, or other blocks that could interrupt or modify the fall.
The exact report command `/fill ~3 ~ ~ ~3 ~45 ~ minecraft:polished_andesite` is not executable in Minecraft 1.4.2. Build an equivalent 46-block-tall solid pillar manually as described below.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher profile configured for the exact version Minecraft 1.4.2, launch the game, and wait for the main menu.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft 1.4.2 main menu is visible.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, open More World Options, set Allow Cheats to ON, and create the world. Leave the seed unspecified and do not select Hardcore mode.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> More World Options... -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: A new singleplayer world has loaded and the player can fly and place blocks without consuming them.

steps.action: Wait until nearby terrain has rendered and player movement responds normally. Find a flat area of solid ground with at least a 7-by-7-block unobstructed landing zone and at least 50 blocks of open air above it.
steps.success_cue: A flat solid landing area and sufficient vertical clearance are available in loaded terrain.

steps.action: While still in Creative mode, clear plants, trees, overhangs, water, or other obstacles from the intended landing zone. Left-click unwanted blocks to remove them. Keep the center and surrounding ground solid and exposed to the sky.
steps.success_cue: The intended landing zone is ordinary solid ground with no block that could catch the player or alter fall damage.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Select Stone, or another ordinary full solid block available in Minecraft 1.4.2, and place it into one of the nine hotbar slots at the bottom of the inventory. Close the inventory and select that hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: An ordinary solid building block is selected in the active hotbar slot.

steps.action: At one edge of the cleared landing area, place one solid block on the ground as the pillar base. Double-tap Space to begin Creative flight. Ascend and place 45 additional blocks directly above the base, one at a time, producing a straight one-block-wide column containing 46 blocks from bottom to top. Aim at the top face of the highest block and right-click to add each next block.
steps.exact_input: double-tap Space; right-click once per block until 45 additional blocks have been placed
steps.success_cue: A straight 46-block-tall solid pillar stands beside the cleared landing zone, equivalent in height to the inclusive Y-to-Y+45 range in the report command.

steps.action: While flying, move above the pillar's top block. Carefully descend until directly over its top face, then double-tap Space to stop flying and settle onto the top block. Do not step off yet.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary on the top face of the pillar, approximately 45 blocks above the ground.

steps.action: Turn so that moving forward from the pillar will send the player toward the center of the cleared solid landing zone rather than toward another structure, water, or the pillar itself.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair faces open air above the cleared landing zone, with solid ground directly below the intended fall path.

steps.action: Press E and verify that all armor slots are empty. Do not equip Feather Falling boots or any other armor. Close the inventory.
steps.success_cue: All armor slots are empty and the player remains standing on the pillar.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Type the Minecraft 1.4.2-compatible game-mode command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command succeeds, the health and hunger HUD becomes visible, and the player is now in Survival mode.

steps.action: Confirm that the health bar is full, no status-effect indicator is present, and the player is still standing on top of the pillar. If health is not full or the player has an effect or armor, reset those conditions before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Survival-mode player has full health, no armor, no status effects, and a clear fall path to ordinary solid ground.

steps.action: Jump outward from the pillar toward the cleared landing zone by pressing Space while holding W briefly. Release movement input after clearing the top block so that no later input changes the test unnecessarily.
steps.success_cue: The player is airborne, descending toward the cleared solid ground, and is no longer above the pillar's top face.

steps.action: Watch the ground approach. While the player is still airborne but close enough that landing would occur almost immediately after resuming—approximately 3 to 6 blocks above the ground—press Esc once. Do not wait until the player has already contacted the ground.
steps.success_cue: The singleplayer pause menu appears while the saved player position is still airborne above the landing zone.

steps.action: On the pause menu, immediately click Save and Quit to Title. Do not choose Back to Game.
steps.success_cue: Saving finishes and the title screen appears; the test world is no longer running.

steps.action: From the title screen, click Singleplayer and select the same test world that was just saved. Do not create a new world or open a different save.
steps.success_cue: The same test world is highlighted in the singleplayer world list.

steps.action: Click Play Selected World, or double-click the selected world, to reload it. Do not open the world through a dedicated server.
steps.success_cue: The loading screen begins for the same world in which the player was saved while falling.

steps.action: As soon as the gameplay view returns, provide no movement, jump, or interaction input. End setup actions immediately so the observation subsystem can monitor the resumed fall and the player's health through the first ground contact.
steps.success_cue: The same world has loaded at the saved airborne position and the player is resuming the fall over the cleared solid landing area without additional input.

stor.handoff_condition: The same singleplayer world has just been reloaded from the save made while the Survival-mode player was airborne near the ground. No post-load movement or interaction input has been given, and the player is resuming the fall toward the cleared solid landing surface. Begin observing the health HUD immediately through the first ground contact.
uncertainties: The report's exact command `/fill ~3 ~ ~ ~3 ~45 ~ minecraft:polished_andesite` was written for a substantially newer command and block registry than the first listed affected version. External version-history verification indicates that `/fill` was added in 14w03a and andesite was added in 14w02a, so neither is available in Minecraft 1.4.2. The plan therefore preserves the commanded inclusive height of 46 blocks but constructs the pillar manually from an ordinary solid block.

The report gives no world seed, coordinates, difficulty, or tower surroundings. A disposable Creative-mode setup world, an unobstructed flat landing area, and ordinary solid ground are practical choices rather than report-mandated requirements.

The report applies to both singleplayer and LAN-hosted worlds but excludes vanilla dedicated-server worlds. This plan selects singleplayer because it is the simplest deterministic affected environment and because Esc pauses the integrated singleplayer world while the player is airborne.

The report only says to exit before hitting the ground and does not give an exact remaining height. Approximately 3 to 6 blocks above the ground is selected to make ground contact occur shortly after the world reloads; visual timing may require a retry if the player lands before Esc opens the pause menu.

The historical command `/gamemode 0` is used to enter Survival mode in Minecraft 1.4.2. If the installation unexpectedly rejects the command despite cheats being enabled, use the version's game-mode control to enter Survival without changing any other test condition.

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition Minecraft 1.4.5, single-player integrated server, Creative mode, in a new disposable Overworld. A flat or Superflat world is recommended only to simplify construction. No specific seed, coordinates, difficulty, resource pack, graphics setting, or dedicated server is stated by the report.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected version Minecraft 1.4.5 rather than the fix version 24w33a.
Use a new disposable world so the TNT test cannot damage an important save.
Use Creative mode as a practical construction method; the report does not require a particular game mode.
Default controls are assumed: E opens the Creative inventory and right-click uses or places the selected item. If controls have been rebound, use the equivalent bound actions.
Obtain Stone or another ordinary solid building block, TNT, a Water Bucket, a Painting, an Item Frame, and Flint and Steel from the Creative inventory.
Perform the test in a clear area away from mobs, dropped items, or unrelated decorative entities that could obstruct placement or make the target entities ambiguous.

In the recommended historical version, reproduce with the explicitly named Item Frame and Painting targets. Do not require later-added target types such as armor stands or glow item frames for this run.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher installation configured for the exact affected version Minecraft 1.4.5, with no gameplay-modifying mods, and wait for the main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is responsive and identifies the running version as Minecraft 1.4.5.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set the game mode to Creative, and create the world. A Superflat world may be selected under the world options to provide a convenient building surface; no particular seed is required. Wait until terrain has rendered and player movement responds normally.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; optional World Type: Superflat
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded Overworld and can use Creative-mode flight and the Creative inventory.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Locate Stone or another ordinary solid block, TNT, Water Bucket, Painting, Item Frame, and Flint and Steel, then move each item to an accessible inventory or hotbar slot. Close the inventory with E or Esc.
steps.exact_input: Stone; TNT; Water Bucket; Painting; Item Frame; Flint and Steel
steps.success_cue: All six required item types are available in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Move to a clear, approximately 9-by-9-block area of level ground. Remove tall grass or other obstructions from the construction area if necessary.
steps.success_cue: There is enough unobstructed level space for a wall and a small water pit, with no nearby entities that could be mistaken for test targets.

steps.action: Using Stone, build a vertical target wall seven blocks wide and four blocks high. Keep the entire front face accessible; this is the face on which the Painting and Item Frame will be mounted.
steps.success_cue: A solid seven-by-four-block vertical wall is present with an unobstructed front face.

steps.action: Directly in front of the wall, excavate a three-by-three-block pit that is two blocks deep. Place one side of the pit against the base of the wall so the future submerged TNT will remain close to entities attached above the waterline.
steps.exact_input: 3 blocks wide × 3 blocks long × 2 blocks deep
steps.success_cue: A two-block-deep, three-by-three pit touches the base of the target wall and is otherwise empty.

steps.action: Select TNT in the hotbar. Place one TNT block in the center cell of the pit's bottom layer. Do not ignite it yet.
steps.success_cue: Exactly one unprimed TNT block is centered on the floor of the two-block-deep pit.

steps.action: Select the Water Bucket and place water throughout the pit. Continue placing water as needed until the surface is level, the spaces around the TNT contain water, and there is a complete water block directly above the TNT. Do not leave the TNT exposed above the water surface.
steps.success_cue: The TNT is visible at the bottom of the pit and is fully submerged, including a full layer of water above it; the water is contained inside the pit.

steps.action: Select the Painting. Face the front of the target wall above the pit and right-click a wall block immediately above the water surface to place a painting. If placement fails or the selected painting extends outside the wall, clear more wall space or remove and place it again. Do not allow water flow to remove it.
steps.success_cue: A painting is attached to the wall facing the submerged TNT and remains present without touching an obstruction.

steps.action: Select the Item Frame. Right-click an unoccupied wall block near the painting and just above the water surface. Leave at least one free wall block if necessary to avoid overlapping the painting. The frame may remain empty because the frame entity itself is the target.
steps.success_cue: An empty item frame is attached to the wall near the painting, and both target entities are visible from the pit.

steps.action: Verify the completed pre-trigger setup before proceeding: one TNT block is fully underwater, the Painting and Item Frame are still attached above the nearby water surface, and no solid block has been placed between the TNT and the front faces of the targets.
steps.success_cue: The submerged TNT, Painting, and Item Frame are simultaneously present and within the compact test structure.

steps.action: Select Flint and Steel in the active hotbar slot. Stand or fly close enough to reach the submerged TNT, aim the crosshair directly at the TNT through the water, and right-click once. Do not left-click, because Creative-mode left-clicking would remove the TNT rather than ignite it.
steps.exact_input: Flint and Steel; right-click the submerged TNT once
steps.success_cue: The TNT changes into a flashing primed TNT entity, the fuse sound begins, and the primed TNT remains inside the water-filled pit.

steps.action: Immediately stop interacting with the setup and wait for the single primed TNT entity to complete its fuse and detonate. Do not place or break blocks, attack the targets, or ignite additional TNT while waiting.
steps.success_cue: The one TNT detonation has completed and the explosion sound and particles have begun to clear; no post-explosion evaluation has yet been performed.

stor.handoff_condition: The single TNT entity has just detonated while fully submerged next to the wall-mounted Painting and Item Frame. Begin the separate observation phase immediately, without touching the wall, targets, drops, or surrounding blocks.
uncertainties: The report requires building the setup shown in setup.png, but the attachment image itself was not included in the supplied report text and its exact geometry could not be recovered. The compact wall-and-pit arrangement above is therefore a minimum deterministic reconstruction rather than a claim that its dimensions match the attachment.

The report does not specify the target-to-TNT distance, water-container dimensions, world seed, coordinates, game mode, or ignition mechanism. Creative mode, the stated dimensions, and Flint and Steel are practical execution choices.

The first listed affected version, Minecraft 1.4.5, was selected as required. This historical run is limited to the explicitly named Item Frame and Painting targets available for the original reproduction; later-listed affected versions can be used in a separate run if testing later-added entity types is required.

Web verification was attempted only because the attachment-dependent setup geometry was missing. No accessible external source established the exact layout shown in setup.png, so the supplied report remains the source of truth and the reconstructed geometry is explicitly marked as inference.

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft: Java Edition 1.4.2 in a local single-player Creative-mode world on Normal difficulty, using any seed. The test is performed at an active Nether portal in the Overworld. Because the report's supplied /summon command is unavailable in this historical version, a version-compatible Spider Spawn Egg is used to obtain the required spider jockey.
preconditions: The launcher must have a Java Edition 1.4.2 installation available.
Use a disposable world because the procedure requires Nether generation, an active portal, hostile mobs, and repeated spawn-egg attempts.
Use Creative mode so Obsidian, Flint and Steel, a Spider Spawn Egg, building blocks, and a weapon can be obtained without unrelated crafting or exploration.
Set difficulty to Easy, Normal, or Hard; the plan uses Normal. Do not use Peaceful because the spider and skeleton must remain present.
Use default controls or their rebound equivalents: E for inventory, W for forward movement, number keys 1–9 for hotbar selection, left-click to attack, and right-click to place or use an item.
Provide an opaque roof over the test lane so a skeleton rider obtained during daytime does not burn before the portal interaction.

Do not execute the report's supplied command in 1.4.2. Preserve it for reference exactly as reported: /summon minecraft:spider ~ ~ ~ {Passengers:[{id:"minecraft:skeleton",HandItems:[{id:"minecraft:bow",Count:1b}]}]}

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for Java Edition 1.4.2 and start it. Do not select the listed fix version 24w21a or any other version.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is open and identifies the running version as 1.4.2.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, leave the seed unspecified, and create the world. Wait until terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded Overworld area and can fly and break blocks immediately, confirming Creative mode.

steps.action: Open the pause menu with Esc, select Options, and set Difficulty to Normal. Return to the world.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Difficulty: Normal -> Done -> Back to Game
steps.success_cue: The world is active again with the difficulty control set to Normal rather than Peaceful.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Obtain Obsidian, Flint and Steel, a Spider Spawn Egg, an opaque building block such as Stone, and a Diamond Sword. Put them into separate hotbar slots by clicking them or by hovering over each item and pressing a number key from 1 through 9. Close the inventory with E.
steps.exact_input: E; Obsidian; Flint and Steel; Spider Spawn Egg; Stone; Diamond Sword; E
steps.success_cue: The required five items are visible in separate slots in the nine-slot hotbar at the bottom of the screen.

steps.action: Choose a flat, open Overworld location with at least nine blocks of clear horizontal space. Using the opaque building blocks, construct a roof at least five blocks above the floor that covers the future portal opening and a test lane extending at least five blocks in front of it. Keep the floor and sides of the lane unobstructed so the spider jockey can be pushed. The roof is only a protective canopy; do not block the portal opening.
steps.exact_input: Select Stone or another opaque block; right-click to place blocks
steps.success_cue: A shaded, unobstructed area exists beneath an opaque roof, with enough room for a five-block-tall portal and a spider jockey.

steps.action: Under the canopy, select Obsidian and build a vertical rectangular Nether portal frame. Make the outer rectangle four blocks wide and five blocks tall, leaving a two-block-wide by three-block-tall empty opening. A full frame uses four Obsidian across the bottom, three additional Obsidian above each bottom corner for the two sides, and four Obsidian across the top.
steps.exact_input: Select Obsidian; right-click to place a 4-by-5 outer frame
steps.success_cue: A complete upright Obsidian rectangle surrounds an empty opening two blocks wide and three blocks tall.

steps.action: Select Flint and Steel. Aim at an exposed interior face of the Obsidian along the bottom of the empty opening and right-click once to ignite the frame.
steps.exact_input: Select Flint and Steel; right-click inside the frame
steps.success_cue: The entire two-by-three interior is filled with animated purple Nether portal blocks.

steps.action: With no entity being ridden, walk into the purple portal opening. Remain inside it until dimension loading begins. Do not provide movement input during loading, then wait until the Nether terrain and the destination portal have rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the Nether beside an active purple Nether portal, surrounding chunks are rendered, and movement is responsive.

steps.action: Walk back into the active Nether-side portal and remain in it until the return transfer starts. After loading, wait for Overworld chunks and the active return portal to render fully.
steps.success_cue: The player is back in the Overworld beside an active portal, with the covered test lane available and movement responsive.

steps.action: Return to the roofed side of the Overworld portal. Select the Spider Spawn Egg in the hotbar and stand three to five blocks directly in front of the portal opening, leaving a straight route between the target spawn position and the purple portal field.
steps.exact_input: Select the Spider Spawn Egg hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: The Spider Spawn Egg is held in the active hotbar slot, and the crosshair points at a floor block beneath the protective roof.

steps.action: Right-click the floor once to spawn one spider and inspect it immediately. If it is an ordinary spider without a skeleton riding it, select the Diamond Sword, kill only that spider, reselect the Spider Spawn Egg, and repeat this single-spawn process. Stop immediately when one use produces a spider with a skeleton visibly seated on its back. Spider spawn eggs in Java Edition 1.4.2 can produce a spider jockey, but the result is random. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Spider_Jockey?mobile-app=true&theme=false&utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: Right-click once per spawn attempt; left-click with the Diamond Sword only to remove an ordinary spider
steps.success_cue: One living spider jockey is present beneath the roof: a skeleton is visibly seated on a spider, and no unnecessary ordinary spiders obstruct the lane.

steps.action: Select an empty hotbar slot so an empty hand is shown and accidental clicks will not strike the entities. Without attacking either entity, use player-body collision by walking into the spider from the side or rear until the intact spider jockey is positioned directly in front of and aligned with the two-block-wide portal opening. Keep the skeleton mounted on the spider throughout positioning.
steps.exact_input: Select an empty hotbar slot; use W and directional movement controls
steps.success_cue: The living spider and its mounted skeleton remain stacked together on the Overworld side, directly aligned with the active purple portal opening.

steps.action: Stand behind the aligned spider jockey, on the side opposite the portal. Walk forward into the spider and continue applying body collision until the spider's body is centered within and visibly intersects the active purple portal blocks. Do not attack, break the portal, enter the portal yourself, or separate the skeleton from the spider. Stop input as soon as the intact mounted pair is inside the portal field.
steps.exact_input: Hold W until the intact spider jockey intersects the purple portal blocks, then release W
steps.success_cue: The spider and its skeleton passenger are still visibly mounted together and have just been pushed into the active Overworld-side Nether portal field.

stor.handoff_condition: The intact spider-and-skeleton stack has just been forced into the active purple Nether portal blocks on the Overworld side, both entities are still mounted together, and the local chunk is responsive. Hand control immediately to the observation subsystem without moving, attacking, dismounting the passenger, or disrupting the portal.
uncertainties: The first listed affected version, Minecraft 1.4.2, is required as recommended_version by version-selection policy, but the report's supplied /summon command cannot be executed there because /summon was added during the Java Edition 1.7.2 development cycle. The exact report command has therefore been preserved in preconditions but replaced operationally with the 1.4.2 Spider Spawn Egg method. ([zh.minecraft.wiki](https://zh.minecraft.wiki/w/Java%E7%89%881.7.2?utm_source=openai))

Obtaining the spider jockey in 1.4.2 is nondeterministic. The Spider Spawn Egg gained a chance to create a spider jockey in 1.4.2, and naturally/spawn-egg-created spider jockeys occur only occasionally; the executor may therefore need multiple isolated attempts. Stop as soon as the first valid jockey appears. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Spider_Jockey?mobile-app=true&theme=false&utm_source=openai))

The report does not specify game mode, world seed, difficulty, single-player versus dedicated server, portal coordinates, or portal orientation. Creative mode, Normal difficulty, single-player, any seed, and a simple standard portal are practical execution choices rather than asserted bug requirements.

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 16w03a in a local single-player Creative-mode world. Use a default Superflat world to provide unobstructed dry land, and use a non-Peaceful difficulty so the Creeper remains present.
preconditions: Install or select the historical Java Edition snapshot profile for Minecraft 16w03a; do not use the fix version 23w33a.
Use an unmodded client so entity, boat, collision, and explosion behavior are not altered.
Use a local single-player world; the report does not require a dedicated server or multiple players.
Use Creative mode to obtain the required entities and items and to prevent the Creeper from naturally targeting the player while it is being pushed into position.
Set difficulty to Normal or another non-Peaceful difficulty; a Creeper spawned on Peaceful difficulty will not remain available for the test.
Prepare an ordinary wooden boat, one Creeper spawn egg, and flint and steel in separate hotbar slots.
The test boat must be placed entirely on solid dry land, not in water.
Use the plain-boat reproduction in 16w03a. Boat-with-chest and bamboo-raft variants do not exist in this recommended historical version.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation that runs the exact Java Edition snapshot listed as the recommended affected version, then start the game with that installation.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and its displayed version is 16w03a.

steps.action: Open the single-player world list and begin creating a new world.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is open.

steps.action: Change the new world's game mode to Creative. Open More World Options, cycle World Type until Superflat is selected, retain the default Superflat preset, and return to the main world-creation screen.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; More World Options... -> World Type: Superflat -> Done
steps.success_cue: The creation screen shows Creative mode and the default Superflat world type.

steps.action: Create the world and wait until terrain rendering finishes and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded, flat grassy world and can move without chunk-loading pauses.

steps.action: Confirm that the difficulty is not Peaceful. If necessary, open the pause menu and Options screen and cycle the Difficulty button until it displays Normal, then return to the world.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options... -> Difficulty: Normal -> Done -> Back to Game
steps.success_cue: The world is active on Normal difficulty and hostile entities will not be removed because of Peaceful difficulty.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots along the bottom of the screen.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface and the nine hotbar slots are visible.

steps.action: Use the Creative inventory search tab to locate an ordinary wooden Boat, a Creeper spawn egg, and Flint and Steel. Search for "boat", "creeper", and "flint" as needed. For the Creeper item, select the spawn egg whose tooltip identifies a Creeper even if the historical display name is formatted as "Spawn Creeper". Place the three items into separate hotbar slots. Do not select any raft or chest-boat item if testing a later affected version.
steps.success_cue: An ordinary Boat, the Creeper spawn egg, and Flint and Steel occupy three distinct hotbar slots.

steps.action: Close the inventory and select the hotbar slot containing the Boat, using its corresponding number key or the mouse wheel.
steps.exact_input: E, then the Boat slot's number key
steps.success_cue: The Boat item is visible in the player's active hand.

steps.action: Move to an open patch with at least five clear blocks around the intended test point. Aim at the top face of a grass block and use the Boat item once to place the boat directly on the grass. Ensure no part of the boat is touching water.
steps.success_cue: An empty ordinary boat is resting entirely on solid dry land with open space around it.

steps.action: Select the Creeper spawn egg. Aim at the ground approximately two blocks from one side of the boat and use the egg exactly once to create one Creeper. Avoid clicking directly on the boat.
steps.exact_input: Select the Creeper spawn egg slot, then right-click the grass once
steps.success_cue: Exactly one Creeper is standing close to the land-based boat.

steps.action: Select an empty hotbar slot so that an accidental use action cannot create another Creeper or ignite anything. Position the player behind the Creeper so the Creeper is approximately between the player and the empty boat.
steps.exact_input: Select an empty hotbar slot; use W/A/S/D to align
steps.success_cue: The player, Creeper, and boat are aligned, with the Creeper facing or standing toward the boat and the player behind it.

steps.action: Walk forward into the Creeper to push it toward and onto the boat. Continue applying gentle forward movement until the Creeper snaps into the boat's passenger position. Stop moving once it is seated; do not enter the boat yourself.
steps.exact_input: Hold W while colliding with the Creeper, then release W when it becomes a passenger
steps.success_cue: The Creeper is visibly seated inside the boat, the player is outside it, and the occupied boat is still entirely on dry land.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing Flint and Steel. Remain close enough to reach the seated Creeper without entering the boat.
steps.exact_input: Press the Flint and Steel slot's number key
steps.success_cue: Flint and Steel is visible in the active hand while the Creeper remains seated in the land-based boat.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair at the seated Creeper's upper body rather than at the boat or ground, then use Flint and Steel on the Creeper exactly once to start its fuse. Do not strike the Creeper, move the boat, enter the boat, or interact again. If the click places a fire block or mounts the player instead of starting the fuse, reset the boat-and-Creeper setup and repeat this step rather than continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Creeper begins flashing and hissing while it is still seated in the boat on dry land; the observation subsystem must take control before detonation.

stor.handoff_condition: The Creeper's fuse has just been started with Flint and Steel while the Creeper remains the passenger of an ordinary boat resting entirely on dry land. Begin observing the occupied boat through the imminent detonation without performing any further player interaction.
uncertainties: The report does not specify game mode, world type, difficulty, seed, or coordinates. Creative mode, Normal difficulty, and a default Superflat world are practical choices that make the stated push-and-explode procedure deterministic without changing the required boat-on-land condition.

The report does not specify how to make the Creeper explode. Using Flint and Steel directly on the Creeper was externally verified as an available deterministic ignition method and avoids relying on hostile targeting while positioning the Creeper.

The first affected version, Minecraft 16w03a, predates boats with chests, so this plan exercises the ordinary-boat path supported by that version. A boat-with-chest variant would require a separately selected affected version from 1.19 or later and must not replace 16w03a as recommended_version.

The report also lists horse and llama reproduction variants, but the plan uses the simplest primary reproduction associated with the issue title: a Creeper riding an ordinary boat on land. The report separately notes that the horse and llama cases were fixed in 20w18a.
The amount and direction of manual pushing are not specified by the report. The executor should stop as soon as the Creeper visibly becomes a boat passenger.
